brands.name: Toy Boat Surfboards
brands.short_description: Toy Boat Surfboards is the personal shaping label of Santa Barbara surfer, sailor, and creative Trevor Gordon — fast, loose boards known for flowing rail-to-rail performance.

models.name: Flathead Fish
models.description: The Flathead Fish is a purpose-designed board meant to be ridden 3 to 4 inches shorter than your traditional keel fish. It's designed for maximum sensitivity, lift, and drive—pared down into a small, efficient package. This isn't your everyday, every-condition fish. The concept behind the polarizing nose design is that you get the rail line of a longer board for hold and drive while reducing the overall length of the board and its swing weight. That design, combined with the heavy single concave throughout the bottom and pinched rails, gives you tons of lift and a board that can bite the wave. It's a board that surprises me over and over in all the best ways. If you've spent time on a mini Simmons or similar, this hybrid brings a super fun blend to the arena.

models.name: VMG Fish
models.description: The VMG is my take on a traditional San Diego-style fish with some adjustments for my taste. This is the board I ride most often because it is just so versatile. This isn't a chunky, bulky, high-volume fish. It's thinner overall, with a foiled-out nose and tail, and mellower, thin-yet-rounded rails that allow it to hold tight to the wave when turning while still maintaining plenty of float and easy rail-to-rail transitions. There is a little more curve in the outline throughout the back half when compared to a standard traditional fish. This board also works great in the barrel and can be built as a twin or a split-keel-type quad. The bottom shape features a single to tri-plane forward. The VMG stretched up to 7' to 10' is the Lordship model.

models.name: Pluero
models.description: Short for Pleuronectiform. Like a halibut or any asymmetrical fish. This is my high-performance shortboard. Like its name, its template and design change depending on the person and the purpose. More often than not, the toe side is straighter and the heel side is curvier. The toe side has more concave, while the heel side is more subtle. The toe side rail is thinner, and the heel side is fuller. Ride it with two, three, or four fins; sizing ranges from two inches below your height to a step-up mini gun.

models.name: LMNOP
models.description: The LMNOP is an all-rounder, high-performance, fuller-templated board that can be ridden in a wide range of sizes across all types of waves and conditions. Similar to the VMG, it features a tri-plane-style hull that allows for easy transitions and a go-anywhere wave approach. The wide point is centered and normally paired with a quad setup.

models.name: Willard
models.description: The Willard bridges the gap between a midlength and a glider-style board. It is designed for high-speed trimming in the pocket while allowing you to quickly switch gears, turn, and redirect down the line. It delivers a rolly, controlled feel and tons of speed while you ride far up on the board. Ideal lengths range between 7'6" and 8'4", and it's best ridden as a single fin.

models.name: Lordship
models.description: The Lordship is the VMG stretched up to 7'6" to 10' — a longer fish template built for glide, trim, and speed in a wide range of conditions.

models.name: Blood Sausage
models.description: Toy Boat's glider model — a long, trim-focused shape for flowing lines and speed.
